chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Asbat ibn Salim, the mawla of Aban, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! Does the Angel of Death know whom he is to capture?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, it is a decree (sikkak) that descends from the sky: "Capture the soul of so-and-so, son of so-and-so."'

key_terms.صِكَاكٌ: Decrees or written orders descending from heaven

ai.seo_question: Does the Angel of Death know in advance whom he will take?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of death by distinguishing between the Angel of Death's inherent knowledge and his reliance on divine command. The term *sikkak* (divine decrees or tablets) descending from heaven indicates that each soul's extraction is governed by a specific, pre-ordained instruction, emphasizing Allah's precise control over the timing of death rather than the angel's independent agency. This highlights the Shia theological view of *tawhid* in action, where even cosmic agents operate strictly under direct divine mandate.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali AL Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Asbaat Bin Salim, a slave of Aban who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Does the Angel of death know of whom (whose soul) he has to capture?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But rather, it is a deed which descends from the sky: ‘Capture the soul of so and so!’’.
en.sarwar: 21. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from ‘Asbat ibn Salim Mawla Aban who has said the following:

“I said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, does the angel of death know whose soul he has to remove from his body?’ He said, ‘No, he does not know. It is the ascribes who come down from the heavens and say, “Remove the soul of so and so, son of so and so.’””
